{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team 
**From:** In-House Counsel (Customer-side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The risk-allocation core of the document is unusually strong for us: limitation of liability (§21), assignment and change of control (§24), licence grant (§13), Vendor audit rights (§22), auto-renewal and uplift caps (§8), warranties (§19) and Vendor insurance (§18) all meet our preferred positions and require no redline.

The problems are concentrated in two places. First, a cluster of **customer-side commercial restraints** — a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment without reduction or termination rights (§2.1); a disclose-and-match obligation that operates as both exclusivity/ROFR and an MFN against us (§7.2); a 24-month all-territory non-compete and a one-way 24-month no-hire (both numbered §12.4). Each of these sits in walk-away territory, and each directly contradicts §12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment. Second, **three material omissions**: there is no indemnification article at all (the outline jumps from §19 to §21, leaving §9.3's cross-reference to "Section 20.5" broken), no transition-assistance or data-return-and-deletion obligation, and no Customer termination-for-convenience right. The absence of a convenience right is especially acute alongside the take-or-pay commitment.

We also need to fix the governing-law clause: §28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts, which is both outside our accepted list and inconsistent with §28.2, which already confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County.

Finally, one flagged item — the §12.4 no-hire redline — failed verification and requires manual drafting before the markup goes out.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | §21.1 (with §§21.2–21.4, §18.2, §1.5) | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; full Excluded Claims set. No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §24.1 (with §§24.2–24.4, §13.3) | Free Customer assignment to Affiliate/successor on notice; Vendor restricted; no Vendor repricing or termination on our change of control. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 (first clause so numbered) | De facto exclusivity/ROFR for the whole term; no category or time limit; conflicts with §12.3. Walk-away. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | §27.3 (with §§8–10, §7.3, §24.4) | No Customer-payable LDs, penalties or early-termination fees. §2.1 take-or-pay addressed under MINCOMMIT, not double-flagged. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | §13.1 (with §§13.2–13.3, §14.3, §10.1) | Affiliates, contractors and Authorized Users covered; paid-up rights perpetual. §14.2 "revocable" wording noted, constrained by §13.3; ownership issue handled under IP. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §22.1 (with §§22.2–22.3) | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, independent auditor; no system or third-party data access. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | §28.1 (cf. §28.2) | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts; outside accepted list and inconsistent with §28.2 New York forum. Walk-away. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 | Open-ended obligation to disclose and match better third-party offers; no product, term or methodology limits; conflicts with §12.3. Walk-away. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | §2.1 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay expressly without reduction or termination rights; contradicts §12.3. Walk-away. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | §8.2 (with §8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension; uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | §10.1 (cf. §16.5) | Refers to "any agreed transition period" but imposes no assistance duty; no data return in usable format or certified deletion. §16.5 cross-refers to a non-existent Section 11. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | §19.1 (with §§19.2–19.5, §6.2) | Workmanlike and conformity warranties; Hosted Services conformity for the full term (better than preferred); mutual, carved-back disclaimer. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | No Section 20 (outline runs §19 → §21) | No IP or other Vendor indemnity anywhere; §9.3 cross-reference to "Section 20.5" is broken; §§19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 presuppose an indemnity. Walk-away. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §18.1 (with §18.2) | CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber/privacy 5M, workers' comp, term plus one year; insurance does not cap liability. |
| Low | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | §14.2 (cf. §§14.1, 14.3, 14.4, 13.2) | Vendor owns every Deliverable created for us; we get only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. Fails preferred and fallback. |
| Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 (p0046) | 24-month post-term, all-territory competitive ban with no carve-outs; contradicts §12.3. Walk-away. |
| Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 (p0045) | One-way outright no-hire covering every Vendor employee for 24 months, with general-advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs negated. Walk-away. **Redline verification failed — manual drafting required.** |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | §9 (only §§9.1–9.3 exist) | No Customer convenience right anywhere, against a three-year term and USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay. Walk-away. |

---

## Walk-Away Items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature rather than negotiating preferences:

1. **§2.1 — Take-or-pay minimum commitment.** Three years at USD 2,000,000 per year with no reduction or termination rights. Our position: no committed minimum; we pay only for Services ordered or used. Fallback, if pressed: commitment confined to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with shortfalls settled by true-up.
2. **§7.2 — Disclose-and-match obligation (exclusivity/ROFR and MFN).** Breaches two rules independently. Our position: no exclusivity, sole-supplier, ROFR or MFN obligation binds Customer. The proposed cure negates only the mandatory operator, leaving exclusivity running in our favour untouched.
3. **§12.4 — 24-month all-territory non-compete.** Our position: no non-compete, field-of-use or territorial restriction on Customer.
4. **§12.4 — One-way 24-month no-hire.** Our position: no non-solicit binds Customer. Fallback available in the margin if needed: mutual, limited to personnel involved in the Services within the preceding 12 months, 12-month duration, with general-advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs.
5. **Missing Section 20 — Vendor indemnification.** No indemnity of any kind. Our position: Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breaches, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in a new §20.5 (which also repairs the broken §9.3 cross-reference) and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our own breach of law.
6. **Missing §9.4 — Customer termination for convenience.** Our position: 30 days' prior written notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and no Vendor convenience right during a committed term.
7. **§28.1 — Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts.** Our position: New York law, with the §28.2 New York County forum retained.

Items 1–4 are each contradicted by Vendor's own acknowledgement in §12.3 that we made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment. That internal inconsistency is our strongest lever and we should lead with it.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Manually draft the §12.4 no-hire redline.** The automated repair failed verification; this is the only finding without a usable markup. The section number is duplicated in the document (no-hire at p0045, non-compete at p0046), so the edit must be anchored precisely to avoid disturbing the non-compete cure.
2. **Issue the markup with the seven repaired or inserted provisions:** §2.1 (commitment removed), §7.2 (operator negated, single edit resolving both EXCLUSIVITY and MFN), §12.4 non-compete (operator flipped), §14.2 (Customer ownership with Vendor assignment), §28.1 (New York law; Singapore forum deleted), new §9.4 (convenience termination), new §10.3 (transition assistance up to six months at then-current rates, data return in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter), and new §20 (indemnification).
3. **Raise the §12.3 inconsistency in the cover note** and ask Vendor to confirm which of §12.3 and §§2.1/7.2/12.4 it intends to govern.
4. **Flag the drafting defects for Vendor to correct:** duplicate clause numbering at §7.2 and §12.4, the missing Section 20, Section 23 with no operative text, and §16.5's cross-reference to a non-existent Section 11.
5. **Confirm commercial appetite on §2.1** before the call. If the business needs a committed spend to secure pricing, we should go in at the fallback (12-month, reducible, true-up) rather than concede the three-year structure.
6. **No action required** on §§8, 13, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24 or 27.3 — these meet our preferred positions and should be protected from erosion in any Vendor counter-draft."}
